Analysis: Pancreatic Cell Loadings

Ziang Zhang

Data and analysis question

We analyze semi-NMF loading factors from pancreatic cells. We sample at most 500 cells per cell type with seed 1, retain cells measured with inDrop3, and select factor columns 3, 8, 9, 12, 17, 18, 20, and 21. This gives 865 cells by 8 factors. We fit \(M=1\) and \(M=2\) MPCurve models to the same matrix to see what each specified number of orderings captures.

Fitting settings

Both fits use MPCurver 0.3.4, CAVI, an RW2 trajectory prior, \(K=50\) grid positions, and ridge = 0. The \(M=1\) fit starts from PCA; the \(M=2\) fit applies Fiedler ordering independently to both similarity-based feature groups. Exact seeds and iteration budgets are in the reproduction script.

Table 1. Fixed model and initialization settings.
model seed method K rw_q ridge max_converge_iter
M1 20260925 PCA 50 2 0 NA
M2 20260927 fiedler 50 2 0 500

One versus two orderings

The plots below arrange the same loadings according to each fitted sample ordering. The first panel uses \(M=1\); the other two are orderings A and B from the fixed \(M=2\) fit. Colours show the observed loading values, with the same colour scale in all panels. Ordering direction is arbitrary.

Figure 1. Eight semi-NMF loading factors arranged by the inferred cell positions under fixed M = 1 and M = 2 fits.

The absolute Spearman correlations between the \(M=1\) positions and the \(M=2\) positions are 0.968 for ordering A and 0.058 for ordering B. Ordering A closely follows the single-ordering fit; ordering B places cells differently.

Cell-type annotations provide another view of the fitted positions. Each point in Figure 2 is one cell, grouped by its recorded cell type.

Figure 2. Inferred pseudotime for each pancreatic cell, grouped by the recorded cell type.

Feature assignments in the two-ordering fit

Table 2. Posterior ordering probabilities for each selected semi-NMF factor.
factor ordering_A ordering_B assignment
Factor 3 1 0 A
Factor 8 1 0 A
Factor 9 1 0 A
Factor 12 1 0 A
Factor 17 1 0 A
Factor 18 1 0 A
Factor 20 0 1 B
Factor 21 1 0 A

Seven factors follow ordering A; only factor 20 follows B. Most cells have similar fitted positions on B, while a smaller subset spreads across its range. The second ordering is therefore driven mainly by factor 20 in this fit.

Fitting objectives

Figure 3. Within-model objectives: the M = 1 CAVI ELBO and the M = 2 structural objective at T = 1.

Each objective rises during its own fit, and both fits satisfy the normalized per-observation convergence rule. The two panels use different objectives, so their heights cannot be used to choose \(M\).

Reproduce

The reproduction script reconstructs the input matrix and both fits. The saved results include selected cell IDs, fit settings, assignments, and fitted positions.
